issues.title: Context loss becomes a fatal Web shader compilation error
issues.reproduction: Real WEBGL_lose_context on the live Viewer caused GPU-particle recreation to compile against the lost context and permanently stop the program.
issues.rootCause: The context accessor accepted a lost WebGL object, including before the queued DOM loss event.
issues.dispositionRationale: Lost-context accessor returns renderer-unavailable until restoration. Old generated runtime fails the focused regression; current normal/fallback GPU/VFX tests pass. Actual Chrome Viewer survives and recovers by selecting Arin then Party; Fire/Lightning automatically resume GPU rendering. Real audio focus and shutdown checks also pass. An automated Enter attempt did not recover Viewer and is not claimed passed.

issues.title: Quick queued Ctrl+Arrow loses its modifier before Viewer consumes it
issues.reproduction: Actual Chrome receives the whole chord, but released Control is no longer physically held when Get Key consumes the queued arrow; the Viewer orbits instead of stepping.
issues.rootCause: Queued event and live physical held-state were sampled at different times.
issues.dispositionRationale: Shared Key_Event_Held preserves physical Key_Held. Native real window-procedure and generated-Web release-before-poll/focus fixtures pass. Actual Chrome Ctrl+Right/Left steps 550/583/550 ms at H158/V0/zoom-15; native Hit steps 0/33/0 ms at H234/V0/zoom-15. Plain arrow still orbits. 300 shared tests, full Viewer hardening, builds and installed VSIX pass.

issues.reproduction: Frozen equipment hide originally left overlays; actual Chrome exposed mesh visibility restored by actor transforms. The expanded native fixture also reproduced three Dragon forward-seek/resume/clip-cut failures.
issues.rootCause: Visibility and continuity decisions must precede the family freeze return; Dragon had not consumed the explicit seek identity or rebased skipped impact cues.
issues.dispositionRationale: Retained part visibility in b835628 plus existing equipment lifecycle checks pass native and generated Web. Native/Chrome actual frozen weapon/shield hide clears mesh, Fire and rim. The expanded actual-Viewer fixture now proves populated Dragon breath, frozen age retention, forward/backward seek, clip cut, hide/show, reseed, unaffected second Fire owner and suppressed skipped impact versus exactly one continuous cue. Native and exact-console Web runs pass; visible Chrome Party breath at 1202 ms clears on a frozen step to 1235 ms, resumes correctly, and frozen Dragon hide/show has no stale Fire. Shared family independence, once-per-frame advancement and automatic tails retain their existing passing assertions. No combat/save mutation or audible-device claim is implied.
